 Here’s who won local elections around Hampton Roads 
 WHRO | 
 By
 Staff Report 
 Published November 3, 2026 at 11:14 PM EST
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Photo by Katherine Hafner 
 Signs for local candidates outside Bayview Recreation Center in Norfolk on Election Day, Nov. 3, 2026. 
 Look up the winners of seats on councils and school boards from Western Tidewater to the Middle Peninsula and Eastern Shore.
 Southeastern Virginia residents have selected new representatives to serve on governing boards and in top jobs across the region.
 Turnout appeared strong Tuesday as steady streams of voters cast ballots, such as Bob Oberosler at the East Ocean View Community Center in Norfolk.
 He was drawn to the polls by a mix of national, state and local issues, including the proposed 1% sales tax increase to fund school construction.
 “I wasn’t ready to agree on raising taxes for that,” Oberosler said. “A couple of the constitutional provisions, I had a pretty strong view on those. And then I think it’s important to vote in any federal election.”
 Krystol Greene voted at Good Samaritan Episcopal Church in Virginia Beach and said top of mind was “the price of everything.”
 “You can’t complain and not do anything about it,” Greene said. “It’s time for our voice to be heard.”
 Ahead of the election, the Department of Justice had requested access to send observers inside Virginia Beach polling places, and civil rights groups did the same in response.
 The city’s Electoral Board denied the requests . But federal monitors still showed up outside some polling places, as legally allowed, according to state election officials.
 See a full roundup below of local election results as reported by the Virginia Department of Elections, as of 11 p.m. Tuesday. Results are considered unofficial until certified on Dec. 7.
